facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms

concepts.why: The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with angina and ST-segment elevation, indicating acute coronary syndrome.
The patient has a history of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and presents with ST-segment elevation, indicating myocardial infarction.

The patient develops recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, and echocardiography reveals akinesia of all apical segments, leading to suspicion of takotsubo syndrome.
The patient develops recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, indicating ventricular tachycardia.
The patient has a history of hypertension, dyslipidaemia, and smoking, and coronary angiography demonstrates significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis, indicating coronary artery disease.
The patient develops ventricular fibrillation requiring external shocks and cardiopulmonary resuscitation, indicating cardiac arrest.
It explains the uncovered finding of a significantly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction after an ischemic event, such as subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch.

rationales.F02: Patient's history of hypertension, dyslipidaemia, and smoking suggests a high risk for coronary artery disease.
rationales.F03: Prior percutaneous coronary interventions indicate a history of coronary artery disease.
rationales.F08: Patent stents in the circumflex artery and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis suggest coronary artery disease.
rationales.F09: ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3 is indicative of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F11: Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation suggest a life-threatening arrhythmia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, new QTc prolongation to 500 ms, and severely reduced LVEF of 35% with akinesia of all apical segments and hyperkinesia of the basal segments is highly suggestive of Takotsubo Syndrome, especially given the absence of significant coronary artery disease to explain the degree of left ventricular dysfunction.
